finance.compare.intro: In Spain and Italy, the choice between traditional maritime credit and nautical leasing depends mainly on VAT status:
finance.compare.loan_text: The buyer owns the boat from day one with a bank mortgage registered in the maritime registry. Ideal for pre-owned vessels where VAT is already settled.
finance.compare.leasing_text: The leasing institution purchases the vessel and leases it to the user with a purchase option at the end. Suited for new shipyard vessels or export structures.

finance.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
finance.faq.q1: Can non-resident citizens obtain boat financing in Spain or Italy?
finance.faq.a1: Yes. Many Mediterranean marine banks provide loans and leasing to EU and non-EU citizens, provided the vessel stays in designated territorial waters and the applicant provides certified tax documents in their country of residence.
finance.faq.q2: Is a pre-purchase marine survey mandatory for lenders?
finance.faq.a2: For pre-owned vessels, accredited marine credit institutions almost always require an independent hull and machinery survey to confirm market valuation and seaworthiness before disbursing funds.
finance.faq.q3: How does the Spanish matriculation tax (IEDMT) affect financing?
finance.faq.a3: In Spain, vessels over 8 metres in length used by tax residents are subject to the 12% IEDMT tax. Some lenders allow this tax to be included in the financed principal, while others require it to be settled separately upon vessel flagging.
finance.leasing_spain.title: Leasing in Spain
finance.leasing_spain.text: Nautical leasing (leasing náutico) lets a person or a company use a boat while the lessor keeps legal title during the contract. It is often used for boats in charter or company use. Tax treatment depends on your situation, so confirm it with an adviser.
finance.leasing_italy.title: Leasing in Italy
finance.leasing_italy.text: In Italy a boat lease (locazione finanziaria nautica) is common for pleasure and commercial craft. VAT and registration rules apply, and lenders normally ask for a survey report. Confirm the details with an adviser.
finance.documents.title: Documents lenders usually ask for
finance.documents.item1: Independent surveyor report on hull and engines
finance.documents.item2: Two years of company accounts, or personal tax returns
finance.documents.item3: Builder's certificate (new boat) or registry extract (used boat)
finance.documents.item4: Insurance quote or binder for the boat
finance.documents.footer: Nautelo does not lend money and does not hold funds. Rates, terms and the final decision are the lender's.
